Referrals can be made by the, Dental Treatment 
Facility (DTF) or Remote Active Duty Service 
Members (Remote ADSMs) may self-refer for 
routine care as long as the dental treatment is less 
than $750 per appointment or the cumulative 
total is less than $1,500 for treatment plans 
completed within a consecutive 12-month period.  
Authorizations can only be made by a Military 
Dentist and will be tracked by United Concordia.  
Dental Treatment Facility (DTF) 
Referral 
If  the Active Duty Service Member (ADSM) has 
been referred to a civilian dentist from a military 
Dental Treatment Facility (DTF), the DTF (or 
ADSM if  designated by its DTF) will request an 
Appointment Control Number (ACN) from United 
Concordia.  All DTF referrals require an ACN 
provided by United Concordia prior to receipt of  
care.  
To coordinate an appointment, the DTF and/or 
ADSM will complete this step through the Program 
Administrators portal on the home page of  the 
website ( addp-ucci.com ) or by calling Customer 
Service at (866) 984-ADDP (2337).  
The DTF and/or ADSM will also receive a list 
of  randomly selected United Concordia network 
dentists (within the program requirements) from 
which to choose when they receive the ACN.  
However, the DTF/ADSM may also request a 
specific United Concordia ADDP Dental Network 
dentist.  
Find a Dentist
All of  our network dentists are listed on our ‘Find 
a Dentist’ application, which can be accessed via 
our ADDP website.  Find a Dentist will return 
all ADDP Dental Network dentists based on 
the search criteria entered (i.e. zip code, county, 
specialty, address, etc.)  
STAR dentists will be designated with a gold 
star and a “yes” in the STAR dentist column.  
Additionally, an amalgam column will indicate 
which dentists perform amalgam restorations.
Process for Arranging An 
Appointment
Once an Appointment Control Number is received, 
an appointment can be made with a United Concordia network dentist.  Appointments can be 
made using one of  the following methods: 
1. The DTF and/or ADSM can select a dentist 
from the list provided by United Concordia and 
make an appointment.  United Concordia will 
send an email to either the DTF and/or ADSM 
within three working days after the options are 
given to confirm that an appointment has been 
made.
Note: United Concordia’s online system does 
not generate ACNs automatically or in real-
time. A United Concordia representative will 
contact the DTF and/or ADSM with the ACN 
and list of  network dentists. 
2. The DTF or ADSM can contact Customer 
Service at (866) 984-ADDP to make the 
appointment.  An appointment will be made 
at the time of  the call.  An email confirmation 
will be sent to the DTF or ADSM after the 
appointment is made. United Concordia can 
make an appointment for the ADSM during 
the same call in which the ACN is generated.
Providing Procedures, Payment 
Policies and Details 
Dentists may only provide the procedures 
prescribed on the DTF referral.  No alternate or 
additional procedures may be provided without a 
modified DTF referral.  
Dentists will not collect any payment from ADSMs 
at the time referred or later bill the ADSMs for any 
referred covered dental care.
The DTF-Referred ADSM is required to provide 
the following information to the United Concordia 
network dentist at the time of  the appointment: 
• A copy of  the referral form provided by 
the military DTF, which must contain the 
Appointment Control Number that was 
provided by United Concordia  
• Necessary attachments (i.e. charts, x-rays, 
etc.)
• Department of  Defense Form 2813 (if  
required)
 
If  an ADSM elects to receive a non-covered service 
from a network dentist, an approval must be 
obtained from the Military Dentist. After receiving

to pay by the ADSM will constitute a waiver of  
the ADSMs right to be held harmless and will be

with the time, date of  agreement and the ADSM’s

Broken and cancelled appointments
• If  an ADSM is unable to keep an 
appointment, he/she should attempt to 
cancel it through his/her military DTF at 
least 24 hours before the scheduled visit. 
United Concordia should be notified by 
the DTF or ADSM upon appointment 
cancellation or reschedule at (866) 984-
ADDP (2337).
• There will be times when ADSMs are faced 
with extenuating circumstances and may 
not have the opportunity to contact the 
dentist.  Dentists are reminded that if  this 
problem persists they should contact United 
Concordia.   
Emergency care
Emergency dental care does not require a referral 
or Appointment Control Number (ACN). 
Emergency dental care (palliative care) consists 
of  any treatment necessary to relieve pain, treat 
infection, control hemorrhaging or repair broken 
fillings by placement of  temporary or permanent 
fillings (not crowns).  Root canal treatment may 
be needed to relieve the pain and infection, and is 
considered emergency dental care.  
Crowns, bridges and denture procedures are 
not considered emergency dental care, and are 
therefore not covered.  ADSMs electing to receive 
non-covered services as part of  an episode of  
emergency dental care are responsible for payment 
of  these services.
ADSMs are encouraged to utilize a United 
Concordia network dentist for emergency dental 
care. Although this is not required, any follow-
up care with a non-network dentist will not be 
authorized, and the ADSM will be responsible for 
payment.ADSM DTF-Referred Subsequent 
Appointments and Modified 
Referrals
Upon receiving treatment, if  a civilian dentist 
finds clinical reasoning for alternative treatment, a 
modified referral is required.  
Referral modifications may be obtained by 
contacting the DTF (contact details are provided 
on the initial referral form).  If  the DTF can not 
be immediately reached, the dentist should contact 
a ADDP Customer Service Representative at 
United Concordia by calling (888) 286-8454.  The 
Referral Modification form will be updated by the 
DTF.  Upon modification, the dentist can perform 
a search in DART®+ (which can be accessed via 
the ADDP website) for the referral modification 
or contact an ADDP Customer Service 
Representative.
The following exceptions apply to this guideline 
and do not require a DTF referral modification:
• Oral evaluation procedure codes: D0120, 
D0140, or D0150 (these may be provided once 
per course of  treatment, per dentist, if  no 
other examination is prescribed).
• 1-2 bitewing radiographic images (D0270 or 
D0272) or 1-2 periapical radiographic images 
(D0220 and D0230) may be added.
• Oral surgeons may perform a D0330 
panoramic radiographic image.
• Amalgam may be substituted for composite 
resin in posterior restoration. 
• One surface may be added or removed from 
a restoration; however, an alternate material 
(resin instead of  amalgam) cannot be provided 
without additional authorization.

adequate substitute for D2752.

ADSMs on Extended Leave
ADSMs requiring civilian dental care, who are 
assigned a military installation with an on-site 
military dental treatment facility (DTF), and are on 
extended leave (e.g., block, terminal, returning from 
deployment) more than 50 miles from their DTF, 
must contact United Concordia prior to receiving 
care.United Concordia will confirm the ADSM’s 
status, assign an Appointment Control Number 
(ACN), and offer assistance in scheduling an 
appointment with a network dentist.Dental offices 
treating DTF-assigned ADSMs on extended leave 
should follow claim submission and authorization 
guidelines for the Remote Active Duty Dental 
Program.

consecutive 12-month period. The procedure must 
be a covered benefit.  Self  referred procedures must 
be a covered benefit.  
Whether or not the Remote ADSM requires an 
authorization for procedures, he/she must obtain 
an Appointment Control Number (ACN) from 
United Concordia before making an appointment with a civilian dentist. The Remote ADSM can send 
an Appointment Request through the Members’ 
portal of  the ADDP website ( addp-ucci.com ) 
or by calling Customer Service at (866) 984-
ADDP (2337). Appointment Control Numbers 
are required before receiving care for covered 
procedures. This includes initial, annual and 
continuation of  dental care.
 
When the Remote ADSM receives an Appointment 
Control Number, they will also receive a list of  
United Concordia network dentists from which 
to choose. Or, the ADSM may request a specific 
network dentist (Refer to the ‘Find a Dentist’ 
section, to see where specific dentists are located on 
our website).
Appointments can be made using any of  the 
following methods:
• The Remote ADSM can make an appointment 
with a United Concordia network dentist by 
contacting Customer Service at (866) 984-
ADDP (2337). An appointment will be made at 
the time of  the call and an email confirmation 
with the Appointment Control Number will 
be sent to the ADSM after the appointment is 
made. 
• If  requesting an appointment online, the 
Remote ADSM will be sent a list of  three 
randomly selected network dentists from United 
Concordia. The Remote ADSM may also 
request a specific dentist when requesting the 
appointment.  The network will send an email to 
the ADSM three working days after the options 
are given to confirm that an appointment has 
been made. The Remote ADSM should contact 
United Concordia with the date and time of  
the appointment, so his/her records may be 
updated. .
Remote ADSMs should not be billed up front for 
any covered procedures and should contact United 
Concordia before seeking reimbursement.
Remote ADSMs are responsible for notifying their 
command of  all dental care received. 
Not all procedures are covered under the 
ADDP . Prior to electing to receive non-covered 
procedures, Remote ADSMs must receive an 
authorization. Authorizations MUST include all 
required radiographs, narratives and diagnostic 
materials. Separate narratives are not required for

Remote ADDP Emergency 
Procedures
Emergency dental care does not require an 
authorization or appointment control number. 
Emergency dental care procedures are defined under 
the Remote ADDP as: 
• Emergency dental care (palliative care) consists 
of  any treatment necessary to relieve pain, treat 
infection, control hemorrhaging or repair broken 
fillings by placement of  temporary or permanent 
fillings (not crowns).  Root canal treatment may 
be needed to relieve the pain and infection, and is 
considered emergency dental care.  
• Crowns, bridges and denture procedures are 
not considered emergency dental care, and are 
therefore not covered.  Remote ADSMs electing 
to receive non-covered services as part of  an 
episode of  emergency dental care are responsible 
for payment of  these services.
• It is recommended that Remote ADSMs utilize a 
United Concordia network dentist for emergency 
dental care. Although this is not required, follow-
up care with a non-network dentist will not be 
authorized.  
Remote ADDP Subsequent 
Appointments and Authorizations
Authorizations are required for all care that the 
Remote ADSM cannot self-refer. If  the Remote 
ADSM is located in an area that does not have 
a network dentist, all care (regardless of  cost or 
treatment category) must be authorized by a Military Dentist, unless the treatment qualifies as emergency 
dental care.  
Authorizations MUST include all required 
radiographs, narratives and diagnostic materials. 
Separate narratives are not required for each  
procedure code; One narrative providing the treating 
dentist’s status for the services provided should be 
included with the claim. Progress notes addressing 
the services provided are also acceptable. Narrative 
information can be included in the Notes section or 
attached as a separate document in the Attachments 
section of  an eClaim in DART®+. Most attachment 
formats are acceptable, including .pdf  and .jpeg. 
The Defense Health Agency (DHA) is requiring 
this additional documentation to ensure it becomes 
part of  the ADSM’s health record and is accessible 
to DHA and the referring DTF. Authorizations 
and all required attachments (i.e. radiographic 
and diagnostic materials) can be submitted online 
through DART®+, which can be accessed via the 
‘Civilian Dentist’ portal of  our ADDP website. 
Upon accessing DART®+, dental offices will be 
required to enter their ADDP Patient Data Tracker 
login and password to access the authorizations 
screens.   
While we highly recommend authorizations 
be submitted via DART®+, alternatively an 
authorization form can be printed and mailed.  The 
Authorization Request Form can be accessed via the 
ADDP website.
A dentist will be required to obtain an authorization 
if:
• Treatment is greater than $750 per 
appointment;
• The cumulative total is $1,500 or more 
for treatment plans completed within a 
consecutive 12 month period;
• The procedure is not a covered benefit  
under the Remote ADDP .
Proposed treatment and pertinent documentation 
must be submitted with all authorization requests.  
The following exceptions apply to this guideline and 
do not require an additional authorization:
• Oral evaluation procedure codes: D0120, 
D0140, or D0150 (these may be provided once 
per course of  treatment, per dentist, if  no other 
examination is prescribed).

To complete dental claims forms for the ADDP , refer 
to the instructions below.

dental treatment

N
Beginning May 23, 2007, use of the NPI became a governm ent mandated requirement for electronic health care 
transactions.  As of May 23, 2008, the NPI was required on all electronic health care transactions.  United Concordia will 
not accept electronic health care transactions (claims, inquiries, etc.) without an NPI.  In addition, individual states may 
require use of the NPI for paper claims. To minimize potentia l claim processing errors and delays in payment, United 
Concordia encourages all dentists to obtain NPIs.   
WHERE CAN DENTISTS APPLY FOR AN NPI?   
Here are three simple ways to apply for your NPI: 
1.Follow the online process at: www.nppes.cms.hhs.gov .
2.Download the paper application from the Web site.
3.Contact the NPI enumerator at (800) 465-3203 or customerservice@npienumerator.com . The application process
isFree.
WHAT ARE ENTITY TYPES? 
When applying for an NPI, cho ose one o r both of the entity types listed below: 
Entity Type 1 (Individual) is defined as any individual dentist, in cluding a sole proprietor, providing health care
services.  Apply using your Social Security Number (SSN ).  Only one NPI will be allowed for an individual dentist.
Entity Type 2 (Organization) is defined as an organization providing health care services, such as group practices,
professional corporations, and clinics, including incorporat ed individuals.  Apply using the organization’s Employer
Identification Number (EIN). A dental practice that is incorporated is co nsidered a Type 2 even if it employs only one
dentist. In certain situations organizations may apply for additional (Subpart) NPIs.
The following page is a guide to help you in choosing the type of NPI(s) you may need for your practice.
WHY IS AN ENTITY TYPE 2 IMPORTANT AND DOES OUR OFFICE REQUIRE A TYPE 2 NPI? 
The type 2 represen ts the organi zation which is most likely used for billing purposes.  It would be incorrect for United 
Concordia to match an individual's type 1 NPI to a United Co ncordia Group Practice ID number.  The type 1 NPI belongs 
solely to the individual, similar to a SSN.  If that individual pr ovider leaves the group practice, their type 1 NPI leaves alo ng
with them. Should the group practice be using the departing  individual's type 1 NPI for billing purposes, it would cause 
potential delays in billing and payment as the group would need to update their systems with a new NPI and communicate 
that new NPI to United Concordia for correct matching.  Cont inued use of the type 1 NPI by the group could constitute 
fraud. In addition, since individual dentists frequently work at multiple practice locations, type 2 NPIs representing each 
practice would ensure payment to the correct practice.   
WHAT IS A TAXONOMY CODE AND IS IT THE SAME AS MY NPI?   
The taxonomy code is NOT  an NPI number. The taxonomy code defines the d entist's and/or group's specialty type and is 
usually a mixture of numbers and letters that end with an 'X '. The NPI is ten digits in length and comprised of numbers 
only.
WHEN SHOULD DENTISTS REPORT NPIs TO UNITED CONCORDIA? 
As soon as you receive your NPI, submit it along with your entity type (1 or 2), National Plan and Provider Enumeration 
System (NPPES) confirmation, address, and your United Concordia provider number using o ne of the following three 
methods: 
Website:  www.unitedconcordia.com/pifria/
Email:  ProviderRequests@ucci.com
Fax:   (844)235-7261 
Visit the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services at 
www.nppes.cms.hhs.gov  for more information.

Health Insurance Portability and 
Accountability Act (HIPAA)
The Health Insurance Portability and 
Accountability Act of  1996 (HIPAA) mandates 
standards for electronic data interchange (EDI) 
and code sets, establishes 
uniform health care 
identifiers, and seeks 
protection for the privacy 
and security of  patient 
data.
The overall objectives 
of  HIPAA are to reduce 
paperwork, improve efficiency of  health systems, 
and protect the security and confidentiality of  
electronic information. National Standards for 
electronic transactions are intended to encourage 
electronic commerce as health care dentists will 
be able to submit the same HIPAA compliant 
transaction to any health plan in the United States 
and the health plan must accept it. There will no 
longer be hundreds of  different formats.
The HIPAA regulations do not require a health care 
provider to transmit transactions electronically. A 
health care provider remains free to submit paper 
claims. The HIPAA regulations do require a health 
care provider who uses electronic media to transmit 
health information in connection with one of  the 
HIPAA transactions to do so in compliance with 
the regulations.
Transactions and Code Sets
The compliance date for the Transaction and 
Code Sets standards for most health plans, 
clearinghouses and dentists (known as covered 
entities) was October 16, 2002. However under 
the Administrative Simplification Compliance Act 
of  2001 (ASCA) covered entities could file for a 
one-year extension which if  filed changed their 
compliance date to October 16, 2003. United 
Concordia filed for the one-year extension and 
became compliant with the Transaction and Code 
Sets standards prior to the October 16, 2003, 
compliance date.
HIPAA Privacy:
In December 2000, the Department of  Health and 
Human Services (HHS) issued the final HIPAA 
Privacy Rule. The intent of  this law is to protect a person’s health information from unwanted, 
unauthorized, and/or commercial uses without 
impeding the delivery of  health care procedures 
or payment. The HIPAA Privacy Rule covers 
health plans, health care clearinghouses and those 
health care dentists who conduct certain financial 
and administrative transactions electronically. The 
HIPAA Privacy Rule became effective on April 
14, 2001. Most health plans, clearinghouses and 
health care providers that are covered by this rule 
were required to comply by April 14, 2003. United 
Concordia achieved compliance with the HIPAA 
Privacy Rule prior to the April 14, 2003 compliance 
date. United Concordia is committed to protecting 
our member’s privacy in accordance with all 
applicable Federal and State laws.
HIPAA Security:
The final HIPAA Security Rule was published 
in February 20, 2003. Most health plans, 
clearinghouses and health care providers that are 
covered by this rule were required to comply by 
April 20, 2005. The intent of  this law is to protect 
the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of  
electronic protected health information.
For more information about HIPAA, visit the 
following websites:
• http://www.wpc-edi.com/hipaa -provides 
implementation guides or the x12N 
transaction standards.
• http://www.hhs.gov/ocr/hipaa  – Privacy 
Information from the Office of  Civil 
Rights.

The American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of  
2009 (ARRA) also known as the “Stimulus Bill” 
was enacted on February 17, 2009. ARRA contains 
extensive provisions that collectively are referred 
to as the “Health Information Technology for 
Economic and Clinical Health Act” or “HITECH 
Act”. These provisions include important 
changes to the Health Insurance Portability and 
Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy and Security 
Rules. The Department of  Health and Human 
Services (HHS) is in the process of  issuing 
regulations and other guidance, which will continue 
for several years. United Concordia has achieved 
compliance with the September 23, 2009 “Breach 
Notification for Unsecured Protected Health 
Information Interim Final Rule” of  the “HITECH

Utilization Review
United Concordia’s Utilization Review (UR) 
program is designed to help ensure that procedures 
reported on behalf  of  our members are rendered 
consistent with the provisions of  their benefit 
programs. Because this program can affect any 
dentist who treats a patient covered by a United 
Concordia plan, it is important to understand its 
purpose and how it works. 
The Utilization Review Process
Data Collection & Statistical Analysis 
Post-payment utilization reviews generally begin 
with the identification of  a potential concern. 
Most frequently, the concern is identified through 
statistical analyses and peer comparisons, but can 
occur as the result of  an inquiry or complaint 
received from a patient or another dentist or as the 
result of  discrepancies noted during normal claims 
processing. 
Upon identification, a complete analysis of  
information available internally at United 
Concordia, as well as other relevant information, 
is conducted. This may include a review of  prior 
claim submissions, pending inquiries, or complaints 
and statistical information. 
Professional Consultant Review/Counseling
The analysis may conclude that intervention 
is required.  If  so, intervention begins with an 
educational letter.  The letter cites the dentist’s 
exceeded procedure(s) and/or peer comparison in 
relation to state average. A twelve month update 
is subsequently performed to determine if  the 
educational letter was successful or if  further 
intervention is required.  
If  there appears to be no change in reporting, 
the dentist is sent a letter which includes a peer 
comparison to the procedure(s) in question, along 
with a request for a sample of  patient records. 
The letter always includes the name and telephone 
number of  a contact person and also provides the 
dentist with the opportunity to discuss any clinical 
or dental policy related questions with a Dental 
Director and/or Advisor.
The record review is always conducted by a Dental 
Director or Advisor, who is a licensed dentist. The 
Dental Director or Advisor is asked to review the available clinical records and diagnostic materials 
and render a professional opinion as to whether the 
records adequately document the services reported.
Upon completion of  the record review, the findings 
are provided to the dentist. If  discrepancies are 
identified, the dentist is provided a detailed report 
for review and consideration. If  the discrepancies 
result in an overpayment, a refund may be 
calculated.
Possible Follow-up Actions
• If  the problems do not improve over a period 
of  time, the dentist may be terminated from 
United Concordia network participation
• If  fraudulent billings are identified, the findings 
will be forwarded to the Special Investigations 
Unit for further investigation
The Special Investigations Unit 
(SIU)
The role of  the SIU is to detect and investigate 
alleged fraud for all lines of  United Concordia 
business.  
The National Health Care Anti-Fraud Association 
defines fraud as an intentional deception or 
misrepresentation that the individual or entity 
makes knowing that the misrepresentation 
could result in some unauthorized benefit to the 
individual, or the entity, or to some other party.
Examples of  fraud include:
• Billing for services not rendered  
• Deliberate submission of  a false claim  
• Intentional misreporting of  any of  the 
following:

Regulatory Compliance
Dentists have a responsibility to ensure the claims 
they submit are truthful and comply with all 
contractual regulations. United Concordia realizes 
ethical dentists and their staffs may make billing 
mistakes and errors through inadvertence or 
omission. When United Concordia determines that a 
billing error, honest mistake or omission has resulted 
in an inappropriate payment, United Concordia 
will request that the practice return the payment. 
However, the dental practice will not be subject to 
civil or criminal penalties.
If  a dentist knowingly submits a fraudulent claim, 
United Concordia will rely on federal and state criminal and civil health care fraud laws. These 
laws cover offenses that are committed with actual 
knowledge of  the falsity of  the claim, reckless 
disregard or deliberate ignorance of  the falsity of  
the claim.
Coding and Billing
The following risk areas associated with billing 
have been among the most frequent subjects of  
investigations and audits conducted by United 
Concordia’s SIU:
• Billing for items or services not rendered
• Submitting claims for services that are not 
reasonable or necessary
• Duplicate billings
• Billing for non-covered services as if  covered
• Billing for unbundled services
• Upcoding the level of  service provided
• Identity theft, and
• Routine waiver of  co-payments or cost share
Documentation and Record Keeping
Timely, accurate and complete documentation is 
critical to nearly every aspect of  a dental practice. 
Documentation is also necessary to determine the 
appropriate dental 
treatment for the patient and is the basis for coding 
and billing determinations. Most importantly, 
failure to properly document has the potential 
to compromise good patient care. In addition to 
facilitating high quality patient care, a properly 
documented dental record accurately denotes what 
procedures were provided and why. The dental 
record may be used to validate:
• The site of  service
• The appropriateness of  the services provided
• The accuracy of  the billing
Accurate dental record documentation should 
comply with, at the minimum, the following 
principles:
• The dental record should be complete and 
legible
• The documentation of  each patient 
encounter should include the reason for the
